means: One way into a tool: the interactive door for people, the structured door for agents and scripts.
not: A permission.

means: An interaction written down - keys pressed, screens expected - run on every change, its screens kept as evidence.
not: A recording only: a scene also checks.

means: The commons' system for coordinating work: it takes work, does it, keeps its journal, and talks with whoever drives it - a person or a machine alike - built on ocoeco.
not: runner (says nothing of coordination, the journal or the leases); lab-agent (a place, not a family); the machine's hands (too narrow: it coordinates people too)

means: oco-agent's own sign of life, sent from its working loop after each healthy turn to a dead man's switch outside the machine, which alerts the author when pulses stop.
not: beat (a driver's sign of presence); heartbeat (used loosely for both); ping (any request)

means: A driver says something to another driver, or to everyone; it is kept in order, and carried to whoever can be reached away from a keyboard.
not: notify (one-way, to a person only); message (says nothing of who speaks); post (a tool's word)

means: Whoever drives work through oco-agent - a person (the author, anyone) or a machine (an AI such as Claude) - holding the driver's lease while working; oco-agent treats them alike.
not: the agent (the system itself); the user (people only, while a driver may be a machine); the AI (machines only)

means: The one way a table's file is written - compact JSON lines, declared field order, empty as null, rows in their order - so a change reads as one line.
not: pretty-printed JSON; sorted keys (each would turn one change into many lines)

means: A repository's tables as data in tables.toml: fields, types, rules across tables, and how pages read.
not: schema (SQL's word: a schema in SQL needs a database to mean anything)

means: How a repository's pages read, declared in tables.toml: the index, introductions, groups, order, labels, relations in words.
not: template, theme (they suggest code or style, not what the page says)

means: A rule that needs more than one table: ids unique across tables, a reference that must resolve, every row cited, no mirrored relation.
not: foreign key (SQL's word, and narrower: no citations, no mirrors)

means: The thing a line, a record or a decision speaks of.
When it happened, to the second: a moment.
not: A day alone: that is a date.

means: Where the whole is weakest right now, read from every project's data, to choose the next piece of work.
not: Whatever is loudest.

means: Who did it - a person, an agent, or a program acting by itself - by the name they go by.
One landed piece of work: a branch, one squash commit on main, and its record.
not: changeset (a bundle in Knope, one file in changesets - two meanings); commit (git's unit; a change may take many)

means: An idea a project rests on, with why it matters.
not: What a word means: that is the vocabulary.

means: How one thing bears on another, found by looking: this led to, needed, halted or repeats that - with why, and how it is known. It runs between two particular rows, of any tables, in any stars. Connections on one thread are a red line.
not: relation (declared once for a whole table: a decision may refine a decision); link (how a row is pointed at, in any field); edge, arrow (words of the drawing, not of what is meant)

means: A place of its own that keeps what holds between its stars: its mark says it is a constellation and what it gathers - stars by name, or every star of an owner; a star may be in many. Standing in it, the fulldome shows the constellation. The four stars once of kind lens are constellations: Linux Phones, Rhizome, Mnemonic Vocabulary, Linux package distribution.
not: observatory (looking, not belonging); organization (GitHub's word); the earlier use of lens for a group of projects

means: A shared process that carries work from one state to the next - built, tested, delivered - which projects call, not copy.
not: A template to copy.

means: Chosen by the observatory's keepers to stand in its navigation. Any lens can still be found without it.
not: Approved or owned.

means: An owned fork of someone else's code (Rhizoid's rhizcut): pinned to an exact upstream point, changed only as named patches each written to go home.
not: A divergent copy.

means: A day: year, month and day.
not: A moment: that is at.

means: A choice taken, with why, and with what was rejected.
not: A plan or a wish.

means: What a star's shine can be focused onto: the one thing every surface must be able to do - lay out what a lens brought into focus. The core term; plain text, a terminal, Markdown, HTML and CSS, and whatever someone makes later are surfaces - each a dome made real. A lens knows of no surface.
not: surface (a surface is one dome made real: the dome is what they share); screen, page, output (each names one surface); renderer (a graphics word, and it names a doer where this names what is done upon)

means: Minutes weighted by how draining they were (load 0-10, Borg CR10): five counts as one. A short heavy chore can outweigh a long light one.
not: Time alone.

means: A way to add a row by saying only what a person knows: the rest is supplied, and the row is held to its shape.
A project's whole chain on one page: why it exists, what it must reach, how each step is delivered and proven, what is happening now.
not: A summary.

means: One named value a row carries.

The second face of a lens, and the act: a lens lets data through and brings it into focus - ordered so it can be made out - as Markdown files, HTML and CSS, a terminal, anything. Nothing is made: the same data comes into focus. What is seen is on the fulldome.
not: show, showing (a lens shows nothing: it lets light through); render (a graphics word, from outside the family); resolve (links resolve, and people resolve problems); image (already means a disk or system image here); project, projection (project is the word star replaced); reveal (plain, but not what a lens does)

means: Where a pointing begins: the thing that points.

Every lens, in focus, on a dome: the lens that focuses all lenses onto all their surfaces. The same at every scale - a star's, a constellation's, an observatory's - and on every surface; touched, not watched.
not: board (one lens: the flow of work); room, wall; a lens beside the others (it holds them); a show to sit through

means: A small daily job in each project that writes down what its work produced: commits, releases, test runs.
not: A person keeping records.

means: The part of a lens through which data is taken in: it says the data's place and relations, and how it is entered with ease - what is already there is not retyped, what the computer can supply is not asked. Also a thing so taken in: one row. ocoeco glimpse brings every lens's glimpse together - their subcommands and flags, declared, so that two cannot collide unnoticed: a collision is found when ocoeco is built, never in use. One lens has one glimpse, which may hold several kinds of entry. The word first named (2026-11-11) only the record of work done: that is the glimpse of the lens of work.
not: note (the earlier way, table by table: one had to know the tables and fields); record (plain, but names nothing one can point at); form (says nothing of looking); pulse (oco-agent's sign of life)

means: The observatory's reading of every marked project's tables, every few hours.
not: A copy of the projects.

means: Whether a pointing holds: what it points at is there, in a place in view.
One of the three stretches of a path: working (it does its job), perfection (as good as it should be), ongoing perfection (it stays so).
not: A deadline.

means: The way one thing bears on another, in the words of the link itself - led to, needed, halted, repeats - or the name of the field that holds the pointing.
What a row goes by within its table. With where it is held and its table it names one thing: place/table:id.
not: A number a machine hands out: an id is words one can say.

means: Why a project exists, written by the project itself for someone who knows nothing about it.
not: A feature list, or a summary for insiders.

means: Which of a few named sorts a row is. Each table says its own sorts, and a row is of one.

A way of seeing, and the concrete mechanism for it, with two faces: its glimpse catches data - the data's place, its relations, and how it is entered with ease - and its focus brings it into view, as a structure of Markdown files, HTML and CSS, a terminal, anything. A lens shows nothing by itself: it lets the data through, ordered. It is made once and used by anyone in ocoeco, in their star or constellation: the data and its structure are known, so it just works. One lens defines a piece of data; many may read it. A lens may be made of lenses.
not: view (SQL's word for one query); dashboard, report; plugin (it adds no code path of its own to a star)

means: How draining an action was this time, from 0 (nothing) through 5 (hard) to 10 (maximal), after Borg's CR10 scale of perceived exertion.
not: How long it took: that is minutes.

means: An action done by hand that a tool could do: counted with its minutes and load, and when it was done, until something automates it.
not: Bad work: it is a measure of where a tool would help, not a judgment.

means: The small file (oco.toml) by which a repository says: I am part of the commons, and here are my tables.
not: A badge someone else gives.

means: A step on a path, reached only when its evidence exists.
not: A date or a promise.

means: How long it took, in minutes.
What something is called by people. A place's name says what it is for, after its own name and a colon.
What a pointing is, whatever its field is called: rests on, is for, follows, is about, places, gathers, is part of, fills.
A place for someone's looking: it gathers the constellations, stars and other observatories its owner cares to see. They do not belong to it and need not know of it. Anyone can have one.
not: constellation (belonging, not looking); the one observatory (there are many); OCO (the ecosystem)

means: The part of ocoeco that observes: it finds places by their marks and gathers what they keep - the same act whether a constellation gathers its stars or an observatory gathers constellations and other observatories. It brings the data and the names of the lenses; a render already made may be taken as it is.
not: observatory (a place; the observer is an act of ocoeco); harvest, discover (its earlier names: a farm's word and a search's)

means: The ecosystem that lets anyone keep stars, show constellations and have an observatory: the agreement and its tools - ocoeco, tad, oco-agent, the lens tool. Not an observatory itself.
not: the author's observatory (one of many, made with OCO); open commons (the principle, wider than OCO)

means: The commons' language and machinery: the tables, the mark, the gatherers and the checks - the blood and heart every project lives by.
not: The observatory's website.

means: The table a thing is a row of.
Where a row comes among its fellows: first, second, third.
One shape a lens brings into focus: a question asked of its tables, and how each answer is laid out as a line.
What a project must reach: its milestones on three horizons, each with the evidence that proves it.
not: A plan of dates.

means: What a lens brings into focus, as rows in the order they are laid out: what a surface reads.
not: A screen or a page: those are surfaces a plane is laid on.

means: A repository with a mark. It keeps its own idea, path, workings and work, in its own data.
not: A folder of code alone.

means: The topmost shape of shapes: what a lens brings into focus, cut from the whole down to its places - fulldome, lens, part, line, place. Each piece has exactly one place because it was cut from there. It comes hand in hand with what it is projected onto, as a port with its adapters; it does not check what it projects, only its shape. What the world calls a project is one: what is thrown forward and lands on a surface, with what it came from left out of sight; a star is that source.
not: the act of a lens (that is focus); a surface's text (the projection laid out, no longer a shape); a check of the data (the data's own, and observing's)

means: A look back over a stretch of work by anyone - a person or a machine - saying what they saw, what they learned and what changes because of it; it touches what it is about and may answer another reflection.
not: retrospective (a ceremony at an iteration's end); post-mortem (only after failures); lessons learned (only what went wrong); review (already means code review)

means: What was considered and not chosen, and why - so that it need not be weighed again blind.
A field said to hold pointings: from a row of one table to things of others, with what the pointing is.
The look around before acting: the question asked, what was found in plain words, and the sources it rests on.
not: A list of links.

means: The word first used on 2026-11-12 for what is now called the fulldome; with it went wall, which needs no replacement: a part of the whole is a lens.
not: see fulldome

means: A lens at the edge: how a table's rows are read from a surface - which kind of surface, which part of it, and the shape taken from it.
Done by hand often enough (three times) or heavily enough (30 effort-minutes) that it asks for a tool.
not: Bad, or forbidden: a saturated action is simply the next candidate for automation.

means: What a thing says of itself in its own words: a lens what it shows, a place what it is for, a row its few telling words.

Text as a volume: so many columns of monospaced characters, unwrapped - a surface into which shapes are fitted, each by its own rule, so that nothing reaches past it. It says what it requires of whatever shows it. The terminal is a screen that is shown; a screen written out is a text file meant to be seen as one.
not: text that flows (continuous lines, wrapped as the viewer likes: it promises nothing of how it looks); page (a page flows, and its browser fits it); window, display (the things that show a screen)

means: What an item is a step toward: a milestone, a decision, or another item.

Something that does not fit the whole, said by whoever sees it or read off the work: stale, overlapping, lacking or unclear. It is shown while nothing has come of it, and is answered by seeing what was lacking - not countered.
not: problem, issue (a thing to be solved); mistake, error, being wrong (a failing of someone); bug, defect (a thing in a thing, not a misfit with the whole)

means: A work someone made that a project stands on - a book, a paper, a page - with what is taken from it.
not: Research: a source is what was read, research is the reading and what came of it.

means: What a finding or a decision rests on: each one a source that can be gone to and read.
A place that produces: one idea or project keeping its own ocoeco data, gathering nothing. A git repository today.
not: project (only what has a repository and code); repository (a tool's word, and only where it lives today)

means: Where an item stands, as someone said: open, next, in progress, waiting, done, parked. More and more it is read off what is done, and not said.
Standing on a neighbour of where one stands.
A concept's own text: what it is, in a sentence or two.
not: statement (the word two projects used for the same role, retired 2026-11-11)

means: Where a projection is laid out, and where what someone gives is read back: text, a screen, a page, a terminal, a line typed in a shell, the environment. A surface adds looks, never meaning; and what comes back off it enters through a lens again.
not: view, render (one direction only); interface (says nothing of what it is)

means: Rows of one shape - kept by a place, or read from a surface.
Words as they were written or said, whole and unchanged.
Anything one can stand on - a row, a place, a lens and what it is made of - known by where it is held, its table and its id.
The few words a row is known by where many are listed.
Where a pointing ends: the thing pointed at.
The things a row speaks of, or changed.
Where a driver stood, step by step, as it happened. A record of work reads from it where it was made.
To be said at once, wherever its driver is - not when next looked at.
Where on the web something is: an address one can open.
The words a project speaks and exactly what they mean - and what they do not mean. ocoeco defines the shared words; a project adds its own.
not: Jargon: a vocabulary translates words into plain language.

means: Time spent on nothing while something else runs - a build, a reboot, CI - recorded by the tool that waits, with what was waited on.
not: Manual work: that is effort spent; waiting is effort not spent.

means: Standing on one thing after another, each reached from the last by what it points at or what points at it. It belongs to no surface.
What was seen, said plainly: of a sign, what does not fit.
The thing one stood on: of a record of work, where it was made; of a sign, where it was seen.
The reason, plainly: what would be lost or go unseen without it.
What actually happens: the backlog, the log, and what the gatherers record.
not: The plan of it.

means: How a project's steps are delivered and proven - its tools, checks, gatherers, tests and practices - each tied to the step it serves, with why we care. As in the workings of a clock.
not: A task to do: that is the backlog.
